Gregory of Nyssa
GREG-or-ee NIS-sah
proper noun
Greek Gregorios, “watchful,” bishop of Nyssa in Cappadocia, the youngest of the three Cappadocian fathers.

See also: Gregory of Nyssa

📖 Biblical Definition

Gregory of Nyssa, younger brother of Basil and the third of the Cappadocian fathers, was a thinker of great subtlety who laboured for the Nicene faith. In his books Against Eunomius he defended the full deity of the Son against the bold Arianism of his day, and in his treatise On the Soul and the Resurrection he upheld the resurrection of the body and the life everlasting. For these labours the dictionary honours him. Yet Gregory also drank deeply of the speculations of Origen, and from that fountain he drew the error of the restoration of all things, teaching that in the end even the damned, and the devil himself, should be purged and brought home to God, so that hell should at last be emptied. This the dictionary names plainly as a corruption, contrary to the express word of the Lord, that the wicked shall go away into everlasting punishment, but the righteous into life eternal (Mat 25:46), and shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord (2Th 1:9). Gregory the defender of the Trinity is honoured; Gregory the universalist is refused. His error is a solemn warning that even a great mind, when it leans upon human speculation against the plain word, may overthrow the doctrine of eternal judgment that Christ Himself revealed.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A fourth-century Cappadocian father, defender of the Trinity, but marred by the Origenist error of universal restoration.

GREGORY OF NYSSA, bishop of Nyssa, the youngest of the Cappadocian fathers.

He was the younger brother of Basil of Caesarea.

His books Against Eunomius defended the full deity of the Son.

His treatise On the Soul and the Resurrection upheld the life everlasting.

He fell into the Origenist error of the restoration of all things.

📖 Key Scripture

Mat 25:46 — "And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal."

2Th 1:9 — "Who shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his power;"

Mar 9:48 — "Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched."

Rev 14:11 — "And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

His defence of the Trinity is honoured, but his Origenist doctrine of universal restoration is refused as contrary to the word of Christ.

expand to see more

The corruption to name in Gregory is the Origenist doctrine of the restoration of all things, the teaching that hell shall at last be emptied and even the devil purged and saved. This the dictionary refuses as a plain departure from Scripture. The Lord Jesus, who alone has the words of eternal life, declared that the wicked go away into everlasting punishment, where their worm dieth not and the fire is not quenched, and that the smoke of the torment of the impenitent ascends for ever and ever. The doctrine of eternal conscious punishment is no harsh invention of later ages but the express revelation of Christ, and no speculation of Origen or of Nyssa may set it aside.

What is honourable in Gregory is his defence of the deity of the Son against Eunomius and his witness to the resurrection of the body. The dictionary honours these. But his error is a solemn warning that even a great and subtle mind, when it builds upon human speculation against the plain word of God, may overthrow a doctrine the Lord Himself revealed. The church receives the fathers as witnesses, and weighs every one of them, the greatest not excepted, by the unerring rule of Scripture.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Greek for “watchful,” Gregory of Nyssa names the youngest Cappadocian, sound on the Trinity but Origenist on hell.

Gregory — Greek Gregorios, “watchful.”

He was bishop of Nyssa and brother of Basil the Great.

He was the youngest of the three Cappadocian fathers.

He defended the deity of the Son against Eunomius.

He fell into the Origenist error of universal restoration.

Usage

"Like Gregory of Nyssa, even a great mind may err when it leans on speculation against the word."

"The wicked shall go away into everlasting punishment, but the righteous into life eternal."

"The fathers are witnesses to be weighed by Scripture, the greatest of them not excepted."
